teaser.text: PACCAR makes commercial trucks and earns more when those trucks need parts, financing, leasing and service. Its dollars come in through a network of brands, dealers, lenders and repair channels, then go out to suppliers, workers, factories, lenders and the costs of keeping vehicles on the road.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for PACCAR?

paragraphs.text: The bear case carries 30% probability. The base case carries 52%, and the bull case 18%. The October 2029 bear-to-bull range is $65.36–$168.75. The recovery needs freight and fleet utilization to support replacement demand, production costs controlled and dealer inventory contained. Parts growth and stable PFS credit quality help. Rising finance provisions or continued Amplify delay hurt. The next checkpoint is the third-quarter earnings call on October 27, 2026. PACCAR must turn stronger orders and builds into profitable deliveries while maintaining its margin outlook.

blocks.heading: How much cash does PACCAR really make?

paragraphs.text: Operating cash flow was $4.42 billion in 2025, including $1.49 billion of higher cash provided by wholesale receivables on new trucks in Financial Services. That cash is real, but it belongs partly to lending activity. Free cash flow usually means operating cash flow less capital spending. The memo’s “real” free cash flow also deducts stock-based compensation, which transfers value through shares or options.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for PACCAR today?

paragraphs.text: Price-to-earnings, or P/E, compares the share price with earnings per share. A trailing P/E uses the past year’s earnings; a forward P/E uses an estimate for the next year. The forward multiple is lower because analysts expect earnings to rise. Analysts build those forecasts from truck orders, production, margins, parts sales, and finance income, but investors decide whether to believe them.

blocks.heading: How much does PACCAR pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The dividend base path rises from $1.40 per share to $1.56. The bear case holds at $1.40. The bull case reaches $1.72. The latest regular quarterly dividend is $0.35, and annual dividends rose each year in the supplied five-year record. The forecast excludes the variable $1.40 special dividend paid in early 2026.

Dividends were PACCAR’s main direct return to shareholders. The company paid $2.27 billion in dividends in 2025. It also declared an extra $1.40 per share payable in January 2026. The extra payment shows that distributions can rise when profits and capital needs permit, but it is not a permanent promise.

blocks.heading: Is PACCAR’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is the money left after operating costs and spending on long-lived assets such as factories and equipment. It shows what may be available for dividends, acquisitions, debt reduction or liquidity. From 2021 through 2025, PACCAR generated more free cash flow in 2025 than in 2021 and paid out 62.2% of its 2025 free cash flow to shareholders.

blocks.heading: What is PACCAR’s dividend yield against its price?

paragraphs.text: The tables show the turn: revenue peaked at $35,127.4 million in 2023 before falling to $28,444.8 million in 2025, while deliveries fell from 204,200 to 144,200. Diluted EPS fell from $8.76 to $4.51, while PACCAR’s computed free cash flow—cash from operations minus capital spending—supports a 6.3% yield against a 1.3% dividend yield. Industrial net cash was $9,252.8 million against $15,636.3 million of finance-arm borrowings in 2025.

blocks.heading: What has PACCAR guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Management’s 2026 heavy-duty market ranges are 230,000–270,000 trucks in the U.S. and Canada and 290,000–330,000 registrations in Europe. South America’s range is 100,000–110,000. These are market forecasts, not PACCAR delivery targets. PACCAR guides to 3.0%–5.0% Parts sales growth and $700.0–$750.0 million in capital investments. R&D guidance is $450.0–$480.0 million.

blocks.heading: What has PACCAR's revenue and profit done lately?

paragraphs.text: Revenue was $7.55 billion in the quarter to June 2026, while net income rose to $752.0 million from $723.8 million. Diluted earnings per share rose to $1.43 from $1.37. Stronger production rates and better operating effectiveness helped, while firmer freight conditions supported truck orders.

blocks.heading: What should investors watch in PACCAR's next results?

paragraphs.text: The nearest checkpoint is the third-quarter earnings call on October 27, 2026. Investors should listen for changes in order strength, production, margins, and the full-year market and spending outlook. Stronger freight rates can help carriers replace older trucks; weaker freight or higher costs can delay purchases.

Finally, PFS credit provisions should be watched alongside freight conditions. If demand becomes deliveries, the battery plan gains a credible path, and customer payments stabilize, PACCAR should be able to fund its next phase without losing sight of the risks around it.
